newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ceyhan tanks hold one mln tonnes Iraqi oil - official.
newsitem.headline: Ceyhan tanks hold one mln tonnes Iraqi oil - official.

text.p: Iraq has about one million tonnes of crude oil ready to export in storage tanks at Turkey's Ceyhan Mediterranean oil terminal, a Turkish pipeline official said on Tuesday.
"There are about one million tonnes (7.3 to 7.5 million barrels) of Iraqi oil in the 12 tanks at Ceyhan," said the senior official, who asked not to be identified.
Each of the 12 tanks at Ceyhan terminal has a capacity of 135,000 tonnes, which gives a total volume of about 11.8 million barrels.

Asked if the twin pipelines from Iraq could handle the 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) mooted as a possible export volume, the official said: "Yes, it can. It worked almost at half capacity last time."
During the first six month tranche of oil exports under the U.N.'s oil-for-food plan Iraq pumped out crude at a rate of around 660,000 bpd.
"Now that the United Nations gave the approval, pumping for Iraq may begin next week," he said.
He did not know of any tanker yet contracted to lift Iraqi oil from Ceyhan.

The United Nations approved Iraq's aid distribution plans on Monday after a delay of about two months. Iraq can now begin oil exports worth about $2 billion for a second six-month term to buy humanitarian goods.
With the delay, Iraq has about a month to sell oil worth $1 billion in the first part of the scheme.
That means exporting about 1.5 to 1.6 million bpd through Ceyhan and the southern Gulf terminal of Mina al-Bakr, or forego some of its allowance.
Analysts say Iraq's oil in Ceyhan could be used for initial sales of an expected 1.3 million bpd.
